news.excerpt: The emergency reforms — zero withholding tax, zero capital gains — are India's bid to join the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index and reverse $29 billion in foreign outflows.

news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Reliance and Meta Are Building India's First Hyperscale AI Data Centre. It Will Run on Seawater.
news.excerpt: The 168-megawatt facility in Jamnagar marks Meta's first built-to-suit data centre in the country, powered by renewables and cooled with desalinated seawater — and Reliance will run the whole thing.
news.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, Chairman of Reliance Industries, who called the deal a 'transformative moment' for India's digital infrastructure
news.nri_angle: India hosting physical AI infrastructure for a $1.5 trillion American tech giant marks a shift from services to foundational computing. For NRIs tracking India's tech trajectory, this puts the country in the same conversation as the US, Ireland, and Singapore for hyperscale data centres.

news.title: Zoho Just Built Its Own Server From Scratch. In Nagpur.

news.image_caption: Zoho Corporation headquarters in Chennai, the parent company behind the Nathu La server platform
news.nri_angle: For NRIs in tech who have spent careers building infrastructure for American hyperscalers, Zoho designing competitive hardware in Nagpur — not Bangalore or an IIT incubator — is both validation and a statement about India's Tier 2 cities.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.excerpt: Pro-Khalistan graffiti, a theft, and broken windows — the wave of vandalism targeting Hindu worship spaces in Northern California has the community demanding answers and installing cameras.

nri-world.nri_angle: For Indian Americans in the Bay Area — home to one of the densest concentrations of Hindu temples in the US — the attacks strike at the heart of community life, turning Sunday worship into a security calculation.

nri-world.image_caption: Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata, headquarters of the central bank's eastern operations
nri-world.nri_angle: For NRIs who have parked dollars in low-yield savings accounts abroad, the RBI's move creates a rare arbitrage window — higher returns than US Treasuries, with the central bank eating the currency risk.

nri-world.title: Twenty-One Years and a Ton of Tamil Granite Later, Berlin Has One of Europe's Largest Hindu Temples

nri-world.nri_angle: Germany's Indian population has surged 70% since 2020 to 260,000, and the Sri Ganesha Temple — built entirely by the Tamil diaspora through donations and voluntary labour — is the most visible symbol yet that the community has moved from survival to permanence.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Lagaan Turns Twenty-Five, the Goodness Gracious Me Gang Reunites, and London's Indian Film Festival Has Never Been Bigger

nri-world.image_caption: Aamir Khan, whose In Conversation session closes the London Indian Film Festival 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: For 1.8 million British Indians, LIFF is the rare festival that takes South Asian cinema as seriously as any national cinema — and the 2026 edition, with its Lagaan anniversary, Goodness Gracious Me reunion, and AI showcase, captures a diaspora confident enough to celebrate its past and invest in its future.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: From Bellevue to Brooklyn, Indian Restaurants Are Opening at a Pace America Has Never Seen

nri-world.image_caption: An assortment of Indian dishes including curries, naan, and biryani — the kind of spread Americans are increasingly seeking out
nri-world.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora built the customer base, the talent pipeline, and the cultural familiarity that now allows Indian cuisine to scale in mainstream American food culture — from fine dining to fast-casual to ghost kitchens.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Is Counting Its People — and Their Caste — for the First Time in 95 Years. Every NRI Should Be Paying Attention.
nri-world.excerpt: The 2027 Census will reshape parliamentary seats, reservation quotas, and welfare targeting. For a diaspora rooted in the south, the numbers could rearrange everything they thought was settled.
nri-world.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi fills out the self-enumeration form for Census 2027, the first census to go fully digital
nri-world.nri_angle: Most NRIs originate from southern states that fear losing Lok Sabha seats in delimitation. The census will also shape reservation policy, property rights, and welfare — all areas where NRIs maintain deep personal and financial stakes.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: One in Four Indian Americans Has Been Called a Slur Since January. A Landmark Survey Maps What Happens Next.
nri-world.excerpt: Carnegie's 2026 Indian American Attitudes Survey reveals a community that isn't just enduring hostility — it's quietly reorganising daily life to avoid it. Nearly a third have stopped discussing politics online. One in five has stopped wearing Indian dress in public.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian Americans celebrating cultural identity at a community gathering
nri-world.nri_angle: The survey captures something rarely quantified about diaspora life: the daily calculus of visibility, where Indian Americans decide how visibly Indian to be in public spaces as discrimination concerns reshape civic participation, dress, travel, and political expression.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: America's Oldest National Indian American Council Just Turned Twenty. Its Founder Wants the Next Two Decades to Be Louder.

nri-world.image_caption: Indian community members gathering at a cultural celebration
nri-world.nri_angle: NCAIA is one of the few national organisations explicitly built to unite the diverse Indian American community across regional and generational lines — its 20th anniversary gala in Maryland spotlighted how far community infrastructure has come and how much further it needs to go.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Rupee Crossed 95. For NRIs Wiring Money Home, Every Dollar Now Buys a Small Fortune.

nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs sending remittances to India are getting significantly more rupees per dollar, affecting family support, property purchases, and retirement planning for millions abroad.

nri-world.title: Gulf NRIs Are Buying Indian Stocks While Wall Street Runs for the Door. The Numbers Explain Why.

nri-world.nri_angle: Gulf NRIs are taking a contrarian long-term bet on Indian equities even as global institutional money flees, reshaping how diaspora wealth flows into India's capital markets.

technology.title: The Chip Industry Just Broke $300 Billion in a Single Quarter. India Is Barely in the Frame.
technology.excerpt: AI-fueled memory demand sent global semiconductor revenue to a record, with NAND up 96% in Q1 2026. For Indian engineers building the chips and NRI investors holding the stocks, the boom is real — but India's share of it remains vanishingly small.
technology.image_caption: Close-up of electronic microchips on a circuit board
technology.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers work at TSMC suppliers, memory giants SK Hynix and Micron, and design houses across the semiconductor stack. NRI portfolios are heavily exposed to chip stocks. Meanwhile, India's own fab story — Tata Dholera, Micron Gujarat — is still years from production. This market milestone frames the gap between where Indian talent sits and where Indian manufacturing stands.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Ambassador Just Ran a Tech Diplomacy Blitz in Washington. Quantum and Physical AI Were on the Table.
technology.excerpt: Vinay Kwatra met with Walmart, the Special Competitive Studies Project, and counter-terrorism officials in a single sweep — signaling that India-US tech cooperation is moving from talking points to trade routes.
technology.image_caption: Vinay Mohan Kwatra, India's Ambassador to the United States
technology.nri_angle: India-US tech ties directly shape the diaspora's professional and investment landscape. Deeper cooperation on AI, quantum, and supply chains could mean more cross-border roles, expanded R&D centers in India, and better regulatory frameworks for NRIs working at the intersection of both economies.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Just Froze Starlink's Launch. The Iran War Is the Reason.
technology.excerpt: Bloomberg reports that India's security agencies have withheld final clearances for Musk's satellite internet service. Starlink says the story is wrong. Either way, rural broadband for 1.4 billion people is stuck.
technology.image_caption: Starlink satellite constellation trails photographed from the Cerro Tololo observatory
technology.nri_angle: NRIs who hoped Starlink would bring reliable internet to their families in rural India face an indefinite wait. The freeze also stalls Jio and Airtel satellite partnerships, affecting diaspora-backed telecom investments.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Tata Electronics Wants a $30 Billion Chip Empire. The Dholera Fab Is Just the Start.
technology.excerpt: From a Gujarat wafer fab to advanced packaging in Assam, the Tata Group is building India's most ambitious semiconductor play. For NRI engineers in the chip industry, the career calculus just changed.
technology.image_caption: Natarajan Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons, at the India Economic Summit
technology.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian-origin engineers work at Intel, TSMC, Micron, and Samsung fabs worldwide. Tata's $30B play creates a credible return-to-India path in semiconductor manufacturing for the first time, plus a new investment thesis for NRI portfolios tracking India's industrial ambitions.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Tech Mahindra and NVIDIA Built a Sovereign AI Lab. It Speaks Bhojpuri.
technology.excerpt: Project Indus 2.0 is an LLM trained on Hindi and dozens of its dialects. Backed by NVIDIA's enterprise stack, it is India's most serious attempt at AI that works for the 600 million people Silicon Valley's models ignore.
technology.image_caption: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, whose enterprise AI stack powers Tech Mahindra's new Center of Excellence
technology.nri_angle: For NRI engineers building LLMs at Google and Meta, Project Indus 2.0 poses a professional question: could India-specific AI become a career track? For NRIs sending money home via UPI or using Hindi banking apps, sovereign AI determines whether those services actually work in their parents' dialect.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Zoho Just Unveiled an India-Designed Server. The Hardware Sovereignty Play Is Real.
technology.excerpt: The Nathu La server was built by a team in Nagpur, cuts power by 18%, and owns every patent in India. Sridhar Vembu's company is done importing its infrastructure.
technology.image_caption: Zoho Corporation headquarters in Chennai, India
technology.nri_angle: Indian tech sovereignty has been a software story for decades — Zoho is making it a hardware story. NRI engineers who've watched India's chip and server dependency grow will recognise this as a significant inflection point. The Nagpur talent pipeline is a direct challenge to the assumption that deep hardware R&D requires Silicon Valley.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Infineon Is Betting Real Money on India's Chip Fabs. That Changes Everything.
technology.excerpt: Germany's biggest chipmaker has started transferring packaging expertise to Kaynes and CDIL, and plans to procure from them. India's semiconductor mission finally has a foreign customer.
technology.image_caption: Close-up of a semiconductor chip on a circuit board
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin semiconductor engineers in the US have watched India's chip ambitions from a distance. Infineon's procurement commitment is the first real signal that OSAT facilities in Gujarat and Punjab could create demand — and jobs — that keep the next generation of chip talent at home.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Perplexity's Aravind Srinivas Wants a 2028 IPO. He's Not Waiting for OpenAI to Go First.
technology.excerpt: The Chennai-born CEO says Perplexity's public listing plan stands regardless of how the OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs land. He'd be the first Indian-born founder to take a generative AI company public.
technology.image_caption: Aravind Srinivas, CEO and co-founder of Perplexity AI
technology.nri_angle: Srinivas represents a generational shift in the Indian tech diaspora — from corporate operators (Pichai, Nadella) to AI company founders. A Perplexity IPO would be the first time an Indian-born founder takes a generative AI company public in the US, signalling that the founder path is increasingly open.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: ISRO Just Handed Its Biggest Rocket to the Private Sector. India's Launch Cadence Depends on It.

technology.image_caption: ISRO's LVM3 rocket on the launch pad at Sriharikota during the OneWeb India-2 campaign
technology.nri_angle: NRI investment opportunities in Indian space startups; return-to-India talent pipeline for aerospace engineers at SpaceX and Boeing; India's growing weight as a commercial launch partner in the Artemis Accords

technology.title: Arvind Krishna's IBM Just Bet on Google's AI. The Multi-Billion-Dollar Play Is Enterprise Plumbing.

technology.image_caption: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna at a company event in 2025
technology.nri_angle: IBM employs 150K+ in India; Google Cloud Practice generates work for Bengaluru/Hyderabad delivery centres; Krishna's reinvention of IBM is a significant Indian-origin CEO transformation story; H-1B implications for cloud/AI consulting roles
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The Tokenpocalypse Is Here. Indian Engineers Are on the Front Line.

technology.nri_angle: Indian H-1B engineers at FAANG rely heavily on AI coding tools now facing cost pressure; Indian IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) face margin squeeze from token costs; open-source model deployment skills become structural advantage for Indian engineers

lifestyle-health.image_caption: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention headquarters campus in Atlanta, Georgia

sources.label: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health / de Beaumont Foundation Public Health Listening Lab Poll 2026
American Psychiatric Association May 2026 Mental Health Survey

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians in America rely heavily on CDC guidance for childhood vaccinations, travel health, and disease alerts. Many first-generation immigrants came from a system where AIIMS and ICMR guidance carries institutional weight. The collapse of CDC trust creates a unique dilemma for NRI families who split time between India and the US, where immunisation schedules differ and the CDC was the tiebreaker.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Ultra-Processed Foods Raised Cancer Survivors' Death Risk by 60 Per Cent. The Tobacco Playbook That Built the Industry Is Now Public.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 15-year study shows UPFs sharply increase cancer mortality. A separate paper reveals US tobacco companies used cigarette-marketing tactics to push the same products worldwide.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Ultra-processed foods in consumer packaging — a new study links their consumption to a 60 per cent increase in cancer survivors' mortality risk (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: American Journal of Public Health — Fazzino et al. 2026
Frontiers in Nutrition — UPF and mortality cohort study 2026

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The traditional Indian kitchen is one of the lowest-UPF diets in the world, but second- and third-generation Indian Americans have shifted heavily toward packaged foods. The Indian grocery aisle — frozen parathas, instant upma, ready-to-eat dal — uses the same industrial processes as Western UPFs. For NRI families, the gap between home-cooked and packaged desi food is a health fault line hiding in plain sight.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk
